candidates.titulo: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
candidates.resumen:
A hacker broke into more than 100 websites using an army of AI agents that mostly operated on their own, according to findings from the AI security firm Norforge. Though Norforge doesn't name the targets, Reuters reports that the victims included companies like John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins.

candidates.titulo: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts
candidates.resumen: OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent that's become a popular alternative to Claude Code and Cursor. But hackers got into part of its online platform and stole some users’ API keys, and the AI tools it turned to for help kept refusing to look at the malicious code.

candidates.titulo: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again
candidates.resumen: Fed up with ads, tracking, and sluggish interfaces, some smart TV owners are turning to AI agents to strip away bloatware and take back control of their TVs.

candidates.titulo: Replika’s founder built the AI assistant she pitched at Disrupt 12 years ago
candidates.resumen: Eugenia Kuyda's newest startup Wabi is positioned to take advantage of an idea she had more than a decade ago. Wabi offers a personal AI assistant with a twist, free and downloadable to anyone today.

candidates.titulo: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
candidates.resumen: Nvidia is leaning hard into the trend of enterprise companies wanting to run their own open models in their own data centers and also trying to make on-device, private AI agents a thing.

candidates.titulo: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
candidates.resumen: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.
